verdict.line: You lose straight poke exchanges before level 6 when Parrrley chips you for free; you win once Hextech Ultimatum (R) is up and his Remove Scurvy (W) is down.

brief.thesis: Gangplank's Parrrley (Q) is a 625-range, 5-second-cooldown poke he can throw all day while Camille has nothing at that range until she lands a telegraphed Tactical Sweep (W), so pre-6 trading favors him by default. Camille's answer isn't out-poking him, it's Hextech Ultimatum (R) at level 6: a dash that anchors him to the fight so he can't kite back to Parrrley range, which is why the matchup settles back to a near-coinflip 50.5% over 2200 games despite OP.GG crediting him the lane.

theirWindow.when: Parrrley (Q) off cooldown while you approach
theirWindow.what: Don't walk a straight line into his pistol range — he's refreshing Parrrley every 5 seconds and will poke you for free the moment you close distance without a wall or minion to break line of sight.

yourWindow.when: his Remove Scurvy (W) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Remove Scurvy clears CC and heals him on a 22-18s cooldown, so bait it out with a feint or chip damage first; once it's down, Hookshot (E) knockup into Hextech Ultimatum (R) locks him to the fight with no cleanse available.

start.why: 51.4% win rate over 1538 games and the majority pick — the regen and damage reduction on autos offset the chip from Parrrley poke and Grog-Soaked Blade poison while you're waiting to reach 6.

boots.why: 50.9% over 1832 games, 80.8% pick rate — his whole early kit is auto-attack poison stacking plus Parrrley, so flat auto-attack reduction matters more than tenacity here.

core.why: First item in the highest-performing path (58.1% over 632 games) — the move speed and proc damage let you actually close the gap he's trying to keep open.
Second in the same path — sustain and AoE damage for extended skirmishes once you're forcing fights instead of dodging poke.
Most common third item (47.2% pick in the top path) — bleeds his burst/poison damage over time so you survive to out-sustain him in longer trades.

situational.when: you're winning fights but dying to burst once he all-ins with allies
the game is going long and you need Hextech Ultimatum back faster for repeated picks
his team is stacking magic damage or CC beyond just Gangplank's poison

runes.keystoneWhy: Procs off your autos in melee trades for max-health scaling damage and healing, which directly answers Grog-Soaked Blade's poison DOT — short trades net in your favor instead of just bleeding health to his passive.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is the top performer at 51.2% and the clear majority pick (68.7%) — Ignite caps the healing from Remove Scurvy and punishes any overextension he makes to land Parrrley, while Flash lets you dodge a poke or force a Hextech Ultimatum engage he can't walk away from.

playing.title: Don't trade before W lands
playing.detail: Tactical Sweep (W) has a delay and 610 range — throw it first and only commit to melee once its outer-cone slow and heal have actually landed, or you're just walking into free Parrrley damage.

playing.title: Bait Remove Scurvy early
playing.detail: Force him to burn Remove Scurvy (22-18s cooldown) on a feinted engage or poke exchange before you commit your real all-in, since it clears CC and heals him on demand.

playing.title: Shield blocks autos, not poison
playing.detail: Adaptive Defenses shields you against his basic attack damage type, but Grog-Soaked Blade's poison is magic damage and ticks straight through that physical shield — don't assume full mitigation in extended trades.

playing.title: Use R to deny his kite
playing.detail: Hextech Ultimatum dashes to him and anchors him to the area, stopping the walk-back-and-reset pattern his Parrrley trading depends on — look for this the instant he commits to a fight at level 6+.

playing.title: Save E for the wall, not the poke
playing.detail: Hookshot (E) requires a wall and is your main engage/escape on a 16-12s cooldown — don't waste it chasing a single auto when you could be setting up a full E-into-R combo.

playing.title: Ignite cancels his sustain
playing.detail: Landing Ignite before he can heal with Remove Scurvy caps his recovery in all-ins, which is often the difference in a lane that's genuinely close to 50/50.

playing.title: Respect Raise Morale near his jungler
playing.detail: If his jungler is nearby and he fires Raise Morale (20s cooldown, buffs nearby allies' AD and move speed), expect an immediate dive — hold Hookshot (E) toward your own wall instead of using it aggressively.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, boots, summoners, and all win rates are pulled from measured OP.GG data on the current patch (16.19.1, 2200-game sample); the power-curve timing and trade reasoning are my own tactical read of the two kits.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of Gangplank’s (Q) when he has Grasp of the Undying! Destroy his Powder Keg(E) with a quick [Q]-basic attack when engaging him!
